message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a residential tenant in Texas. (The information reflects the Texas Property Code as of the last update in 2024; always check for any recent amendments or local ordinances that might apply to your specific city or county.) | Category | What You’re Entitled To | Practical Tips | |----------|------------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may charge a maximum of **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Get a written receipt and keep a copy of the lease.
• Ask for a “security‑deposit ledger” that lists any deductions. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (e.g., functioning plumbing, heating, electrical, pest control).
• The landlord must repair any major defects that affect health or safety. | • Document problems with photos and written notices.
• If repairs are not made within a reasonable time, you may withhold rent or pursue a “repair‑and‑deduct” remedy (see §92.006). | | **Notice Requirements** | • For a **month‑to‑month** tenancy, the landlord must give **30 days’ written notice** to terminate.
• For a **fixed‑term** lease, the landlord can only terminate at the end of the term unless you breach the lease. | • Keep a copy of any notice you receive.
• If you receive a notice that seems too short, you may challenge it in court. | | **Rent Increases** | • There is **no statutory limit** on how much a landlord can raise rent, but the increase must be **reasonable** and **not discriminatory**. | • Ask for a written explanation of the increase.
• If you suspect discrimination, file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office. | | **Privacy & Entry** | • The landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24–48 hrs) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of all entries.
• If the landlord enters without notice, you can file a complaint. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on **race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income** (e.g., public assistance). | • If you believe you’ve been discriminated against, file a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights. | | **Eviction Process** | • The landlord must follow the **Texas Property Code §92.001–92.006**: provide a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for non‑payment, 30‑day notice for lease termination).
• You have the right to contest the eviction in court. | • Respond promptly to any notices.
• If you’re facing eviction, consider contacting a tenant‑rights organization or legal aid. | | **Repair‑and‑Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major defect, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from your rent (up to the amount of the defect). | • Keep receipts and document the defect. | | **Lease Modification** | • Both parties must agree in writing to modify the lease. | • Never sign a new lease that changes your obligations without reviewing it carefully. | | **Legal Assistance** | • Texas has several tenant‑rights groups (e.g., Texas Tenants Union, Legal Aid of North Texas). | • If you’re unsure of your rights, consult a lawyer or a local tenant‑rights organization. | ### Quick Reference Checklist 1. **Security Deposit** – Verify the amount and get a written receipt. 2. **Move‑in Inspection** – Take photos, note any existing damage, and have the landlord sign the inspection report. 3. **Notice of Repairs** – Send a written notice if you spot a problem; keep a copy. 4. **Rent Payment** – Pay on time; keep receipts or bank records. 5. **Lease Terms** – Read the lease carefully; ask questions about any ambiguous clauses. 6. **Dispute Resolution** – If you disagree with a landlord’s action, start with a written complaint; if unresolved, consider mediation or small‑claims court. --- #### Useful Resources | Resource | What It Offers | Link | |----------|----------------|------| | Texas Property Code | Statutory text on landlord‑tenant law | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/ | | Texas Attorney General – Housing | Tenant‑rights guides, complaint forms | https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/ | | Texas Commission on Human Rights | Discrimination complaints | https://www.tchra.org/ | | Texas Tenants Union | Advocacy, legal referrals | https://www.texastenantsunion.org/ | | Legal Aid of North Texas | Free legal help for low‑income tenants | https://www.lantex.org/ | --- **Bottom line:** As a Texas tenant, you have the right to a safe, habitable home, a fair security‑deposit process, reasonable notice before entry or termination, protection against discrimination, and a clear, lawful eviction procedure. Keep all documentation organized, communicate in writing whenever possible, and seek legal help if you encounter any violations.
